atlas_home_region_card.compact: The late-1960s heavy guitar road where blues-rock, psychedelia, distortion, and extended soloing push toward hard rock and metal.
atlas_home_region_card.standard: It is one of the clearest bridges from 1960s pop-rock into 1970s hard rock, heavy metal, and arena guitar identity.
atlas_home_region_card.deep: The late-1960s heavy guitar road where blues-rock, psychedelia, distortion, and extended soloing push toward hard rock and metal. It is one of the clearest bridges from 1960s pop-rock into 1970s hard rock, heavy metal, and arena guitar identity.

region_scene_page.compact: Hendrix, Cream, The Doors, Steppenwolf, and related bands took the blues-rock base of the British Invasion and made it louder, darker, and more exploratory.
region_scene_page.standard: Hendrix, Cream, The Doors, Steppenwolf, and related bands took the blues-rock base of the British Invasion and made it louder, darker, and more exploratory. The Doors' Break On Through (To the Other Side), The Jimi Hendrix Experience's Fire, Steppenwolf's Magic Carpet Ride, and Blue Cheer's Summertime Blues give the scene its high-recognition landmarks.
region_scene_page.deep: Hendrix, Cream, The Doors, Steppenwolf, and related bands took the blues-rock base of the British Invasion and made it louder, darker, and more exploratory. Compared with psychedelic pop, it is less cute and less compact. The Doors' Break On Through (To the Other Side), The Jimi Hendrix Experience's Fire, Steppenwolf's Magic Carpet Ride, and Blue Cheer's Summertime Blues give the scene its high-recognition landmarks. From there, the examples move from quick recognition toward medium and deeper scene signals.

mission_detail_history_module.compact: What this route tests: The late-1960s heavy guitar road where blues-rock, psychedelia, distortion, and extended soloing push toward hard rock and metal.
mission_detail_history_module.standard: Hendrix, Cream, The Doors, Steppenwolf, and related bands took the blues-rock base of the British Invasion and made it louder, darker, and more exploratory. The sound can be riff-heavy, organ-haunted, feedback-soaked, or jam-driven, but it usually keeps a blues pulse under the psychedelic surface. It helps place this road in a broader music-history context.
mission_detail_history_module.deep: Hendrix, Cream, The Doors, Steppenwolf, and related bands took the blues-rock base of the British Invasion and made it louder, darker, and more exploratory. The sound can be riff-heavy, organ-haunted, feedback-soaked, or jam-driven, but it usually keeps a blues pulse under the psychedelic surface. It is one of the clearest bridges from 1960s pop-rock into 1970s hard rock, heavy metal, and arena guitar identity.
